title: Desert Glassback Burrower
tests: Generated via GPT Image 2 shell CLI; exact output path verified before append; JSON parse and public R2 URL verified after append.
prompt:
Design a believable salt-pan desert creature called the Desert Glassback Burrower with a reflective heat-shield carapace, dew-collecting belly bristles, and a sand-gold shell with violet shadows, shown as a realistic natural-history creature study. Create a richly detailed square natural-history studio-and-habitat study of one adult and two smaller juveniles at the edge of a cracked white salt pan at dawn. The adult is low, broad, shovel-snouted, about the size of a large tortoise, half-emerged from a shallow burrow with loose salt crust pushed aside; its translucent mineral carapace reflects harsh sky light like frosted glass, its digging forelimbs end in dark keratin spades, its protected black eyes sit beneath overhanging shell ridges, and fine belly bristles are visibly beaded with dew. Show juveniles sheltering in the adult's shade, wind-polished salt crystals, tiny desert seed husks, mineral dust, hardy gray-green saltbush shoots, warm dawn rim light, cool violet shadows, and plausible macro field-photography detail. Avoid readable text, labels, prompt cards, fantasy monster tropes, gore, logos, watermark, incoherent anatomy, and generic centered creature-on-blank-background styling.

Reusable fill-in-the-blank template: Design a believable [HABITAT] creature with [ADAPTATION 1], [ADAPTATION 2], and [TEXTURE/COLOR], shown as a realistic natural-history creature study. Make the finished image show [LIFE STAGE OR GROUPING] in [SPECIFIC MICROHABITAT], with visible anatomy, scale cues, habitat traces, material textures, and lighting that explain how the adaptations work without turning the image into a labeled prompt card.

What the reusable visual operation changes or emphasizes: it turns a habitat-and-adaptation brief into a plausible original animal study, emphasizing ecological logic, coherent anatomy, tactile surface detail, scale, and behavior in context.

Optional negative constraints: no readable private data, no logos, no watermarks, no prompt cards, no incoherent anatomy, no generic fantasy monster, no blank specimen backdrop unless requested.

Example substitution: [HABITAT] = salt-pan desert; [ADAPTATION 1] = reflective heat-shield carapace; [ADAPTATION 2] = dew-collecting belly bristles; [TEXTURE/COLOR] = sand-gold shell with violet shadows; [LIFE STAGE OR GROUPING] = one adult with two juveniles; [SPECIFIC MICROHABITAT] = dawn burrow edge on cracked white salt crust.
